title: Audit console: time-travel snapshots, role-aware masking, and CSV/JSON export
creator: Priya Singh
description: Background: Customers and internal SREs need a single audit browsing experience that supports precise investigations across RBAC v2 contexts and SSO session metadata. Existing console search supports basic filters and NDJSON exports but lacks: role-aware column masking, time-scoped snapshot exports (time-travel), and guaranteed exported formats for legal/compliance reviews. Scope: build console search enhancements (advanced filter builders), cursor-based pagination for long result sets, streaming CSV and JSON exports with role-based redaction, saved queries for teams, and an opt-in time-travel snapshotter that captures query state and underlying event cursor to produce reproducible exports.
tasks: Design UX: query builder additions, saved-query modal, export options (CSV/JSON/NDJSON) - design review with PM/SEC
Backend: extend search API to accept snapshot_timestamp and include session/saml context in result rows
Backend: implement role-aware column masks using RBAC v2 policies and OPA hooks
Export: implement streaming exporter that produces consistent CSV header ordering and explicit null markers, supports chunked downloads
Pagination: implement stable cursor-based pagination with opaque cursor tokens and server-side TTL
Saved queries: store encrypted saved queries with team visibility and per-query ACLs
Telemetry/SLOs: add metrics for search latency, export throughput, and mask-failure rates
E2E tests: include RBAC v2 permutations, SAML session context, and large-result exports (100k+ rows)
Docs: update console docs with examples and admin guide for masking and snapshot exports
acceptance_criteria: Console search UI exposes advanced filters (actor, org, resource_type, action, saml_session_id, ip, custom_metadata) and allows saving queries with names and descriptions
Search API supports snapshot_timestamp param; querying at a snapshot returns deterministic results consistent with the exported snapshot
Exports produce two canonical formats: newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) and RFC4180-compliant CSV with explicit column schema header
Export respects RBAC v2 policies: columns marked as sensitive are masked in the export according to role (e.g., full, partial, redacted)
Cursor-based pagination supports stable cursors with TTL >= 24h for snapshot exports and returns next_cursor tokens for iterative retrieval
Large exports stream successfully without loading entire result set into memory; 95th percentile throughput >= 8MB/s for a 100k-row export during standard load
Saved queries can be shared to teams and audited (who created/edited/shared) and appear in the console saved list
Security review completed and design approved by Security and Privacy teams; no high-severity findings outstanding

migration_notes: RBAC v1 exports allowed full columns by default. RBAC v2 introduces policy-driven masks. For existing saved queries tagged before RBAC v2 rollout, we will: (1) attach a compatibility flag and run exports under a migration role mapping; (2) surface a warning in the UI that saved query may yield different columns under RBAC v2; (3) provide an admin tool to regenerate snapshots using the old-role mapping for compliance requests.
performance_targets: Search: 95th percentile latency < 500ms for queries returning <= 100 rows under normal load
Export: sustained server-side streaming throughput >= 8MB/s on p95 for 100k-row jobs
Memory: exporter must keep memory usage < 200MB for 100k-row exports
Snapshotting: snapshot capture time < 3s for up to 5M events if running on dedicated exporter node
